scenario.title: Vendor Meeting and Improvement Action Follow-up
scenario.initial_description: The team meets with an equipment vendor to discuss improvement ideas. After the meeting, someone summarizes the discussion and follows up on action items.

reference_workflow.goal: Coordinate a vendor meeting, capture improvement decisions, and track follow-up actions.

activities.name: Assign action-item owners and due dates

decisions.condition: Is the proposed improvement technically feasible?
branches: feasible
requires revision
owned
owner missing

automation_opportunities.rationale: Meeting scheduling can be assisted by calendar availability checks.
Meeting notes can be summarized into decisions, open questions, and action items.
Action-item reminders and status tracking can be automated.

activities.name: Extract and Log Action Items
outputs: Action item list with owners and due dates

activities.name: Assign Action Item Owners
outputs: Assigned action items with responsible parties and deadlines

activities.name: Collect Action Item Completion Evidence
activities.system: Task Management System / Document Management System

activities.name: Escalate Unresolved Action Items
outputs: Escalation notice to vendor or senior management

decisions.condition: Are all required attendees available for the proposed meeting time?
branches: Yes - confirm meeting and proceed to agenda preparation
No - reschedule and re-invite

decisions.condition: Is the action item completed by the due date?
branches: Yes - collect completion evidence and close item
No - send follow-up reminder or escalate

decisions.condition: Is the completion evidence sufficient for closure?
branches: Yes - close action item
No - request additional evidence or corrective action

decisions.condition: Has the action item remained unresolved past escalation threshold?
branches: Yes - escalate to vendor or senior management
No - continue monitoring

exceptions: Vendor cancels or reschedules meeting at short notice
Key stakeholder unable to attend; meeting may need to be postponed or proceed with delegate
Meeting notes are incomplete or disputed by attendees
Action item owner becomes unavailable (e.g., leave, role change); item must be reassigned
Vendor fails to deliver on committed action items; escalation or contract review required
Improvement idea requires budget approval before action item can be completed

automation_opportunities.rationale: Meeting scheduling can be automated using calendar integration tools that check availability of all required participants and propose optimal meeting slots, reducing manual back-and-forth coordination.
constraints: Requires calendar system integration with vendor's external calendar or manual confirmation
Time zone differences may complicate automated scheduling

automation_opportunities.rationale: If meetings are conducted via video conferencing with recording, AI-based transcription and summarization tools can generate draft meeting summaries, reducing manual effort and improving consistency.
constraints: Requires participant consent for recording
AI summaries require human review for accuracy before distribution
May not capture non-verbal context or informal agreements

automation_opportunities.target: A5 - Extract and Log Action Items
automation_opportunities.rationale: Natural language processing can identify and extract action items from meeting summaries or transcripts and automatically populate a task management system, reducing manual data entry errors.
constraints: NLP accuracy may vary; human review required
Ambiguous action items need clarification before automation

automation_opportunities.rationale: Once the meeting summary and action item list are finalized, automated distribution via email or collaboration platform can be triggered without manual intervention.
constraints: Human approval of summary content required before automated send
Distribution list must be maintained and accurate

automation_opportunities.rationale: Task management systems can automatically track due dates, flag overdue items, and generate progress dashboards without manual monitoring effort.
required_data: Action item list with due dates and owners
Task management system with reporting capability
constraints: Action item owners must update task status regularly for monitoring to be accurate

automation_opportunities.rationale: Automated reminder notifications can be sent based on configurable rules (e.g., X days before due date, on due date, and X days after if incomplete), eliminating the need for manual follow-up.
constraints: Overly frequent automated reminders may cause notification fatigue
Escalation logic must be carefully configured to avoid premature escalation

automation_opportunities.target: D2 - Is the action item completed by the due date?
automation_opportunities.rationale: This decision can be automated by querying task status in the task management system at the due date and automatically routing to reminder or closure workflows accordingly.
constraints: Relies on timely and accurate status updates by action item owners

automation_opportunities.target: D4 - Has the action item remained unresolved past escalation threshold?
automation_opportunities.rationale: Escalation rules can be codified and automated within the task management or workflow system, triggering escalation notices without manual intervention after a defined overdue period.
constraints: Escalation thresholds must be agreed upon and configured in advance
Edge cases (e.g., item pending vendor response) may require human override

assumptions: The team uses a digital calendar system that supports availability checking for scheduling purposes.
A task management system is available to log, assign, and track action items.
Meeting notes are captured in a digital document management system rather than paper-based records.
The vendor meeting may occur in-person or via video conferencing; the workflow accounts for both.
Action items may be assigned to both internal team members and vendor representatives.
The improvement ideas discussed relate to equipment used by the team, not to general organizational processes.
A single team member is responsible for note-taking during the meeting, but the team lead is responsible for review and approval of the summary.
Follow-up cadence and escalation thresholds are defined by the team lead or organizational policy.
The workflow repeats for subsequent vendor meetings, with prior action item status informing the next meeting agenda.
Budget approval or procurement steps, if needed for action items, are handled outside this workflow scope.
